messages.subject: Re: rjava -- are inner classes supported?
messages.body_plain:
On Nov 2, 2006, at 11:41 AM, Vincent Kraeutler wrote:

> hi,
>
> i seem to be unable to instantiate inner classes in rJava.
>
> doing
>
> .jnew("fully/qualified/class/name")
>
> works fine, but
>
> .jnew("fully/qualified/class/name/inner")
>
> fails. neither the documentation nor google seem to know anything  
> about inner class support in rJava. am i just not trying hard  
> enough, or is this expected behaviour?
>

Well, both :). Inner classes are referenced as ParentClass$InnerClass  
in Java. Also you must supply the outer class to the constructor as  
well. So for

public class A { public class B { } }

You can instantiate it as follows:

a=.jnew("A")
b=.jnew("A$B",a)

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I encounter an exception while submitting an R command using Java R client
interface.

I have debugged it but do not feel well to try to solve it.
The exception occurs in line 238-239 (Java R client release 503):
	    for(i=0;i<b.length;i++)
                rq[i+4]=b[i];

Exception is "java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException - 853"
The exact command I submitted is below between "----" lines:
I hope this informations will help someone reproduce and solve it.
Thanks in advance for some reply
Luc
-----------------------------------------------------
out<-file("D:/dev/java/tomcat/webapps/GED/log/RServe.log","w");sink(file=out);tryCatch({setwd("D:/dev/java/tomcat/webapps/GED/temp/analysis/7734247")
library(affy)

#Read pheno data
pd <-read.phenoData("pheno.txt",header=TRUE)
af <- ReadAffy(phenoData=pd)

#Normalization
#TODO eset<-gcrma(af);
eset<-rma(af);

#Comparison
#TODO : Faut il appliquer les étapes préalables expliquées dans
#	http://www.bioconductor.org/workshops/2002/Summer02Course/Labs/basics.pdf
anova_fuc <- function(y) anova(lm(y~Origin))
res <- esApply(eset,1,anova_fuc)
#TODO : utiliser library(genefilter) ; ? genefilter ; ?Anova
capture.output(res,file="anova_result_7734247.txt");

#Output normalized expression
capture.output(exprs(eset),file="normalized_expression_7734247.txt");

#Free objects

messages.subject: Re: R or Perl-based client for Rserve?
messages.subject_clean: R or Perl-based client for Rserve?
messages.body_plain:
David,

On Nov 8, 2006, at 12:27 AM, David Reiss wrote:

> does anyone know of a perl- or R-based client that has been written  
> for Rserve?

R-based client doesn't make much sense to me (save for academic  
interest), because then you don't need Rserve at all (R has both  
serialization and socket support - see also snow's SOCK  
implementation for R processes talking to each other). As of perl, I  
remember someone giving it a shot, but I've never heard of it being  
finished.

However, if all you want is to just use R from a perl process for  
batch computation (e.g. in cgi), you may consider using the C++  
client, more precisely the rcmd example which runs an arbitrary  
script via Rserve and returns the result. Also it should be fairly  
easy to incorporate the same functionality into perl directly using XS.

Finally, if you don't need the client/server approach, you may want  
to have a look as RSPerl.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: JRClient exception
messages.body_plain:
Simon,

Thanks for your quick answer, and sorry to have forgotten the name of the java
class in which the exception occurs. It is Rtalk.java

You do not need any of the underlying data to reproduce this bug since exception
occurs BEFORE to submit the command to RServe.

I have written two little debug Java classes.
ReproduceBug1.java reproduces it with an R connection (although it just send a
remark to R server)

ReproduceBug2.java reproduces it without R connection.
In this class, I have extracted from Rtalk the method throwing exception.
I have modified it to add some debug traces.
All modifications are not indented in order to distinguish modifications from
original code.

>>From my point of view, the origin of the bug is located here (Rtalk.java lines
229-230) :
                byte[] b=par.getBytes(Rconnection.transferCharset);
                int sl=par.length()+1;

Since afterward it is b array that is copied, we should compute sl not from
par.length() but from b.length. Since there is a translation because of UTF8
encoding, their lengthes may not be equal if some characters with accent by
instance appear in the String).

By the way, would it be possible to get rid of the try/catch block contained in
this method. Except because of bugs (like this one ...), this part of code
should not throw any exception. We could either get rid of it, or report
proprely of the nature of the exception (Classname, message).

Hope all this will this time help you understand the problem I encountered.

Luc

messages.body_plain:
Phil,

my largest file was a 65MB file with 2.5mio rows and 7 cols, which
takes about 15 secs on my PM G5.

What makes loading a long job are alpha-numerical variables with
very many categories, as parsing and checking categories for existence
is expensive.

If it took you 9mins, I guess you either have a distinct name for all  
the 560k
items or your PB did start to swap, which slows the procedure very much
down.

Martin

messages.subject: Re: Install problem
messages.body_plain:
On Nov 21, 2006, at 6:22 PM, Werner Wernersen wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I tried to install JGR 1.4-6 on Windows but I get an
> "Can't find R home in
> registry." error. I just used the default install from
> R 2.4.0 so I don't know
> what could have gone wrong.
>
> Has anybody an idea?
>

If you don't have write permissions in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE then R  
installer possibly didn't set the path. Please start the registry  
editor (Start  -> Run ... -> type "regedit"), and look for Software\R- 
code in both HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE and HKEY_CURRENT_USER. If you find  
it, please export it and send me the output.

Thanks,
Simon
